'''José Fernando F. Mendes''' (born in [[Porto]]) is a [[Portugal|Portuguese]] [[physicist]] (statistical physics) and [[Professor#Other positions|professor]] of physics, best known for his work and contributions to the field of [[network theory]]. Graduated from [[University of Porto]] in 1987.{{cn|date=September 2026}} He earned a PhD in March 1995 from the same University under the direction of Eduardo Lage, the title of the thesis was "Dynamics of spin systems".{{cn|date=September 2026}}

Mendes was head of the Physics Department from December 2004 to February 2010 at University of Aveiro. From October 2009 to February 2010 he was director of the Associated Laboratory of the Institute of Nanostructures, Nanomodelling and Nanofabrication (I3N) [https://www.i3n.org/].

From February 2010 to February 2018 served as vice-rector for Research and Doctoral Studies at the [[University of Aveiro]]. Was the representative of the Portuguese universities in the Instituto do Petroleo e Gás (Galp) until 2018 [https://www.galp.com/corp/pt/media/comunicados-de-imprensa/comunicado/id/398/instituto-do-petroleo-e-do-gas].

He has been the President of the [[Complex Systems Society]] [https://cssociety.org] (2021 - 2024) and Director of the i3N-Aveiro since September 2023 [https://www.i3n.org/].

==Academic career==

In 1983 he entered the University of Porto and graduated in physics in 1987. He gained his master's diploma in 1990.{{cn|date=September 2026}}
In 1987 he was an assistant in the Department of Physics, University of Porto. As a graduate student he visited as several universities as a researcher, including [[Oxford University]], [[Geneva University]], the [[City University of New York]], and São Paulo.{{cn|date=September 2026}}
After finishing his Ph.D., he became an assistant professor in the same department.{{cn|date=September 2026}} In 1996 he did a one year postdoctoral fellowship in [[Boston University]] under the supervision of Sid Redner. In 2002 did his "habilitation".{{cn|date=September 2026}} In 2002, he became an associate professor at University of Aveiro and in 2005 professor.{{cn|date=September 2026}} He was invited as professor by [[Henri Poincaré University]] (Nancy), Universidade Federal Minas Gerais (UFMG) and visiting researcher at Consiglio Nazionale Delle Ricerche (Pisa), [[Nanyang Technological University]] (NTU), [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] (EPFL-Lausanne) and [[ETH Zurich]] (Zurich).{{cn|date=September 2026}}

==Awards==
Member of The [[Complex Systems Society]].<br />
[[Fellow of the American Physical Society]] in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2003&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|publisher=APS|access-date=15 September 2020}}</ref><br />
Litoral Awards Prize "Research" (2020) [https://litoralmagazine.com/jose-fernando-mendes-vence-premio-investigacao/]<br />
Senior Prize [https://cssociety.org/community/awards/senior-scientific-award], [[Complex Systems Society]] (2020): "for his seminal contributions and the many further developments of the theory of Complex Networks."<br />
